# enco:plugin@0.16.0

Enco plugin contract. Plugins interact with the host only through it: each exports the
interfaces of its world, and only a tool plugin imports `host`.

## Worlds

### `provider-plugin`

A model service's mapper for completion and embedding.

It imports nothing: the host sends its requests to the endpoint, and records each completion's
response before decoding it.

- Imports: types
- Exports: lifecycle, completion, embedding

### `completion-plugin`

A model service's mapper for completion; it imports nothing.

- Imports: types
- Exports: lifecycle, completion

### `embedding-plugin`

A model service's mapper for text embedding; it imports nothing.

- Imports: types
- Exports: lifecycle, embedding

### `decision-plugin`

A decision service's mapper; it imports nothing.

- Imports: types
- Exports: lifecycle, decision

### `tool-plugin`

A plugin exposing model-facing tools, the only kind that imports host capabilities.

A tool acts while it runs: where it goes and in how many steps is its own logic, and the host
settles each call by its outcome.

- Imports: types, host
- Exports: lifecycle, tools

### `composer-plugin`

A plugin that writes model requests; it imports nothing.

- Imports: types
- Exports: lifecycle, composer

### `channel-plugin`

A messaging protocol's mapper. It imports nothing; the host trusts it with the connection's
account.

- Imports: types
- Exports: lifecycle, channel

Opaque adapter fields: the whole message as the adapter that wrote it replays it.

#### enum `effect`

Mutation semantics used to order calls and settle interrupted work.

Consecutive read-only calls run together; other calls run one at a time. A call cut off by
a crash fails as retryable when it is read-only, and settles as unknown otherwise.

- `read-only`: Changes nothing beyond its result.
- `idempotent`: Making the call again has the same effect as making it once.
- `side-effect`: Changes something that must not be changed again blindly.

#### record `tool-spec`

A tool disclosed to the model.

`input-schema` describes the argument object in a subset of JSON Schema:
- objects with `properties` and `required`, always with `additionalProperties: false`;
- strings with `enum`, `minLength` and `maxLength`;
- integers and numbers with `minimum` and `maximum`;
- booleans;
- arrays with `items`, `minItems` and `maxItems`;
- `anyOf` with two or more schemas.

Any schema below the root may carry a `description` and a `default` that fits it; the root
is an object and carries neither. A declaration outside the subset fails to load. The host
checks every call against the schema before the plugin sees it: an optional property given
as null counts as not given, and an integer written with a zero fraction, such as 5.0,
arrives as 5.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The name the model calls the tool by: ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, unique among the plugin's tools. |
| `description` | `string` | What the tool does, for the model to read. |
| `input-schema` | `json` | The argument object, in the subset of JSON Schema stated above. |
| `effect` | `effect` | What a call may change; completion adapters ignore it, and the host uses it when dispatching. |

#### variant `outcome`

A known result, a known failure, or an external effect that cannot be confirmed.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | `json` | The call succeeded with this JSON result. |
| `failed` | `failure` | The call failed, and its effects are known. |
| `unknown` | `failure` | An external effect may have happened and cannot be confirmed; it is never retried automatically. |

#### variant `unviewable-reason`

Why part of a message is kept only as a description.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `unsupported` | `_` | It is not a file Enco can keep, such as a location or a poll. |
| `unavailable` | `string` | It could not be retrieved, for this reason. |

#### record `unviewable`

Part of a message's content kept only as a description, such as a location or an

Facts about the message, such as who sent it, are not content: one that cannot be read is

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `what` | `string` | A plain description such as report.pdf, voice message or location, not a protocol type name. |
| `reason` | `unviewable-reason` | Why it cannot be shown. |

|---|---|---|

channel's may also be an absolute URL on the base URL's origin or on one of its `origins`.

| `url` | `string` | Where to send it, as stated above. |

| `body` | `option<list<u8>>` | The bytes to send, if any. |
| `timeout-ms` | `option<u32>` | The time limit in milliseconds; the host's default when absent. |

#### func `config`

```wit
config: func() -> json;
```

The configuration of this invocation's generation, excluding credential mappings.

#### func `log`

```wit
log: func(level: log-level, message: string);
```

Write a diagnostic to the host log.

#### func `http`

```wit
http: async func(request: http-request) -> result<http-response, http-failure>;
```

Send a request and collect its response; non-2xx statuses are returned as responses.

The host attaches declared credentials only to the bound origin (scheme, host and port),
overriding the matching request header. Redirects are followed only within that origin.
Cross-origin redirects are returned unchanged. Credential values in response headers,
bodies and failures are replaced with [redacted:<environment variable name>].
Encoded forms of a credential (such as base64) are not redacted.

### `tools`

Model-facing tools whose definitions are fixed with their generation.

#### func `list`

```wit
list: func(config: json) -> list<tool-spec>;
```

Project tool definitions from configuration already accepted by `lifecycle.describe`.

Definitions are fixed with the generation, so this runs without network access.

#### func `call`

```wit
call: async func(name: string, input: json) -> outcome;
```

Execute one tool.

`input` already fits the tool's `input-schema`; validate only what the schema cannot
express. Return an unknown outcome when an external effect may have occurred but is
unconfirmed.

### `completion`

Adapts canonical requests to a model service protocol, as a pure mapper.

The host sends what `encode` returns to the endpoint and records the response before `decode`
reads it, so each settlement can be traced to what the service said.

#### record `request`

The frozen messages, disclosed tools and output budget for one completion.

User messages may include images; tool messages contain one result followed by any images.
The calls of each assistant message are answered right after it, one tool message per call,
whose result carries the call's `id`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `messages` | `list<message>` | The messages, in order. |
| `tools` | `list<tool-spec>` | The tools the model may call. |
| `max-output-tokens` | `u32` | The most tokens the reply may use. |

#### enum `stop-reason`

The service-reported reason that generation stopped.

- `end-turn`
- `tool-calls`
- `max-tokens`
- `other`

#### record `completion`

A completed model attempt.

Canonical parts are text, tool calls and extensions; generated images stay in extensions.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | `message` | The reply, with the `assistant` role. |
| `usage` | `usage` | What the attempt cost in tokens. |
| `stop-reason` | `stop-reason` | Why generation stopped. |

#### variant `complete-error`

Why `decode` returned no completion.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `failed` | `failure` | The request failed. |
| `overflow` | `overflow` | The service turned the request away as too large; a smaller request may succeed. |

#### func `encode`

```wit
encode: func(settings: settings, request: request) -> result<http-request, failure>;
```

The request that asks the service for this completion.

The host sends it to the endpoint only, with the endpoint's credentials, and records the
response before `decode` reads it.

# Errors
`provider.bad_request` when the protocol cannot express `request` or `settings.options`.

#### func `decode`

```wit
decode: func(response: http-response) -> result<completion, complete-error>;
```

What the service's response to `encode`'s request means, whatever its status.

A request that got no response never reaches this function: the host reports it as
`provider.network` or `timeout`.

# Errors
`overflow` when the service turns the request away as larger than the model accepts, as an
HTTP 413 always does. Otherwise `failed`, with the codes `provider.auth`,
`provider.rate_limited`, `provider.server`, `provider.bad_request`, `provider.bad_response`
and `timeout`.

### `embedding`

Embeds texts for retrieval independently of model completion, as a pure mapper.

#### func `encode`

```wit
encode: func(settings: settings, inputs: list<string>) -> result<http-request, failure>;
```

The request that embeds `inputs`; the host sends it as it sends `completion.encode`'s.

# Errors
`provider.bad_request` when the protocol cannot express `inputs` or `settings.options`.

#### func `decode`

```wit
decode: func(count: u32, response: http-response) -> result<list<list<f32>>, failure>;
```

One nonempty vector of finite numbers per input, in input order, all of the same width.

`count` is how many inputs `encode` was given. A response that does not hold that many such
vectors is `provider.bad_response`.

# Errors
The codes `completion.decode` lists for `failed`.

### `decision`

Answers independent questions against shared evidence, without generating messages, as a pure
mapper.

#### record `label`

An option or score level.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The answer's name, unique within its question. |
| `description` | `option<string>` | What the option means, when the name alone is not clear. |

#### variant `question-kind`

A yes/no predicate, an unordered choice, or score levels ordered from low to high.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `predicate` | `_` | A yes-or-no question. |
| `choice` | `list<label>` | One option from an unordered list. |
| `score` | `list<label>` | A level on a scale, from low to high. |

#### record `question`

Instructions and the allowed answer shape for one independent judgment.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `instructions` | `string` | What to judge, for the service to read. |
| `kind` | `question-kind` | The shape the answer takes. |

#### variant `answer`

An answer to one question, as probabilities, or a refusal.

Probabilities are finite and in [0, 1]; choice and score distributions sum to one
within 0.01, allowing for rounding by the service.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `predicate` | `f64` | The probability of yes. |
| `choice` | `list<f64>` | One probability per option, in label order. |
| `score` | `list<f64>` | One probability per level, in label order. |
| `refused` | `_` | The service declined to answer this question. |

#### func `encode`

```wit
encode: func(settings: settings, state: string, questions: list<question>) -> result<http-request, failure>;
```

The request that asks the service to judge each of `questions` against the same text
`state`; the host sends it as it sends `completion.encode`'s.

# Errors
`provider.bad_request` when the protocol cannot express `questions` or `settings.options`.

#### func `decode`

```wit
decode: func(questions: list<question>, response: http-response) -> result<list<answer>, failure>;
```

One answer per question of `questions`, in their order and of their kind.

`questions` are the ones `encode` was given, and the response is the service's to that
request, whatever its status. Any question may instead receive `refused`.

# Errors
The codes `completion.decode` lists for `failed`.

### `composer`

Writes the model requests of the Sessions whose profile names this plugin.

A composition is a pure function of its arguments and its own code, and changes nothing but its
result: a composer imports nothing and has no files or environment variables, and the plugin's
configuration reaches only `lifecycle.describe` and `options-schema`. The wall clock reads the
Round's instant, the monotonic clock stands still and randomness is seeded by the Round, so the
same generation, called again within a Round with the same arguments, returns the same plan.

The host records each plan before sending it and resolves its Log references. A plan breaks
this contract when it discloses a capability outside this Round, refers to a position outside
the transcript, or sends images to a model that does not accept them; when a reply plan leaves
out a capability in `lifeline`; when a plan's output limit is 0 or above its target's budget; or
when a compaction discloses any tool, stops where no Round ends, or leaves no transcript item
after it for the reply to answer.

| `seq` | `u64` | The entry's place within its epoch. |

#### record `compose-input`

Everything the host supplies for one composition.

| `home` | `string` | The home's absolute path on the node running this Round.  Its layout is part of this contract: `config.toml`; the standing instructions, `AGENTS.md` for the owner and `profiles/<name>.md` for each profile; `plugins/<name>/`, `sdk/`, `manual/`, and `workspace/`, the working directory of a new Session. `.data/` is Enco's own store and not part of it. |
| `transcript` | `transcript` | The conversation as it stands, which a plan may refer to.  After a backtrack it is the Log up to the backtrack's target, then everything from the backtrack on, so positions can skip. |
| `previous` | `option<plan>` | The plan of the latest completed reply request in that conversation; absent at the start, or when it could not be read, which `omitted` then says. |
| `compaction-requested` | `bool` | Whether the owner asked for the conversation to be compacted before this Round's reply.  Once this Round records a compaction, it is false for the Round's later compositions. |
| `owner-context` | `bool` | Whether this Session has the owner's context: its profile and every ancestor's give it. |
| `owner-instructions` | `option<string>` | The owner instructions: the text of `AGENTS.md`, as read at the start of this Round.  Absent when the file does not exist, when `owner-context` is false, and in safe mode. |
| `profile-instructions` | `option<string>` | The profile instructions: the text of `profiles/<profile>.md` for this Session's profile, as read at the start of this Round.  Absent when the file does not exist, and in safe mode. Unlike `owner-instructions`, it does not depend on the owner's context. |
| `memories` | `list<memory>` | Memories for this Round in priority order: pinned ones first, then those recalled for the latest input, most relevant first.  Empty when `owner-context` is false, and in safe mode. |
| `omitted` | `list<omission>` | Content the host could not supply; the host records it with the plan. |
| `capabilities` | `list<capability>` | Every tool this Round may disclose; in safe mode, only the lifeline. |
| `lifeline` | `list<capability-id>` | The tools every reply plan must disclose; empty when the Session does not require the lifeline. |
| `unavailable` | `list<unavailable-plugin>` | Plugins left out of this Round. |
| `safe-mode` | `option<safe-mode>` | Why this Round runs in safe mode; absent in normal operation. |
| `reply` | `reply-target` | The model a reply plan is for. |
| `compaction` | `option<compaction-target>` | The summarizing model; absent when no summarizing model is usable. |
| `children` | `list<child>` | This Session's children that are not archived, in creation order. |
| `profiles` | `list<delegable-profile>` | The profiles a new child may use; empty when this Session cannot delegate. |

#### record `compaction`

A request to summarize history before replying.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `upto` | `log-pos` | The last Round end to summarize: one of `transcript.round-ends`, before the latest transcript item, so the reply after the summary has history to answer. |
| `plan` | `plan` | The summarizing request; it discloses no tools. |

#### variant `composition`

What a composition returns.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `reply` | `plan` | A reply request. |
| `compact` | `compaction` | Summarize history first; the host composes again once the summary is recorded. |

#### func `options-schema`

```wit
options-schema: func(config: json) -> json;
```

The JSON Schema of the options a profile passes to `compose`, in the subset `tool-spec`
states.

An empty object must fit it. The host checks a profile's options against the schema of the
generation that runs them: registering configuration or code that breaks a profile's options
is rejected, and a profile whose options no longer fit, as after a rollback, cannot use this
plugin until they do. The schema is fixed with the generation, so this runs without network
access.

#### func `compose`

```wit
compose: func(options: json, input: compose-input) -> result<composition, failure>;
```

Write the next request.

`options` fit the running generation's `options-schema` and are normalized as tool arguments
are. Return `compact` only while `compaction` is present. Each compaction ends at a Round
end the transcript shows and hides it, so a Round's compactions end with its visible
history. When the target a composition is for carries `overflowed`, return a composition
other than that plan: the service behind the target turned it away, and returning it again
breaks the contract.

# Errors
`context.overflow` when no valid request fits the window; when only a compaction would make
it fit and `compaction` is absent, the host records why no summarizing model is usable. The
host records any other code as `compose.failed`.

### `channel`

Translates a messaging protocol as a pure state machine; the host owns connections, timers and credentials.

The host records each external input before handing it over, and carries out what the mapper asks.

#### record `socket`

A WebSocket the host opens and keeps until the mapper asks to reconnect or the connection
stops.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `string` | Where to open the socket: a path on the base URL, or an absolute `ws` or `wss` URL.  A path starts with `/` and joins the base URL with `http` turned into `ws` and `https` into `wss`. An absolute URL must be on the base URL's host and port, or at one of the mapper's `origins`. |
| `close-code` | `u16` | The code the host closes the socket with; a protocol that resumes sessions across reconnects may need one other than 1000. |

#### record `pacing-gap`

The time the host leaves before each message it sends through one connection.

Each field is at most the limit the manual lists for channel `pacing`; a larger gap fails
loading, because stopping a connection waits out a started gap.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `minimum-ms` | `u32` | The least milliseconds from one message finishing to the next one starting. |
| `jitter-ms` | `u32` | Up to this many more milliseconds before each message, chosen at random. |

#### variant `read-step`

How the host reads the protocol next.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | `http-request` | Send this request; its response is one arrival. |
| `socket` | `socket` | Open this socket; each frame on it is one arrival, until it closes. |

#### record `closure`

How a socket ended.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | `option<u16>` | The close code, when the protocol sent one. |
| `reason` | `string` | The close reason, or the host's description of the network failure. |

#### variant `arrival`

Something that reached the mapper through the host.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `response` | `http-response` | The response to the read request. |
| `frame` | `string` | A text frame on the open socket. |
| `closed` | `closure` | The socket closed, by the protocol or through a network failure. |
| `timer` | `_` | The timer the mapper set has expired; its reading can change state and request actions, but has no inbound messages. |

#### record `fault`

What a protocol answer means for the host's settlement and retries.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `failure` | `failure` | What failed. |
| `unknown` | `bool` | The request may have taken effect, so it must not be sent again. |
| `fatal` | `bool` | The whole connection is unusable, not just this request or destination. |
| `retry-after` | `option<u32>` | How long the protocol asks to wait before retrying, in seconds. |

#### record `identity`

The account a connection reaches.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `protocol` | `string` | A nonempty protocol name without colons; with `account`, it keys connection state. |
| `account` | `string` | A nonempty, stable account ID within the protocol, treated as opaque by the host. |
| `facts` | `json` | What the mapper needs to know about the account later, such as the bot's username. |

A conversation's name, as far as the protocol carries it.

| `fetch` | `string` | Fetch this nonempty locator to obtain it; the fetch ends with `fetch-step.name`. |

| `locator` | `string` | The opaque locator passed to `fetch`. |

#### record `inbound`

A message that arrived, as the protocol describes it.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `string` | The protocol's key for accepting this message once, such as an update or event ID. |
| `conversation` | `string` | The conversation, where replies go. |
| `realm` | `option<string>` | The realm this conversation is in, such as a Discord server or a Telegram chat with topics; absent for a conversation on its own.  A realm is what a protocol groups several conversations under; a direct chat or a group without topics is in none. Its ID is nonempty. The owner can declare a realm private to them; its conversations are then private. |
| `conversation-name` | `option<conversation-name>` | The conversation's name, such as a topic's title, when the protocol gives one; the host only uses it to name a Session made for the conversation. |
| `message` | `string` | This message's ID, unique within the conversation. |
| `sender` | `option<string>` | The sender's ID, when the protocol reports one. |
| `sender-name` | `option<string>` | The sender's display name, when the protocol reports one. |
| `direct` | `bool` | Whether the conversation is one to one. |
| `addressed` | `bool` | Whether the message is addressed to this bot; always true in a direct conversation. |
| `reply-to` | `option<string>` | The message this one replies to, or the message a command was invoked on. |
| `respond` | `option<string>` | The handle for answering this message once accepted, when the protocol expects an answer, such as for a command or a button. |
| `action` | `action` | What it asks for. |

#### record `reading`

What the mapper asks of the host after one arrival.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `messages` | `list<inbound>` | Messages to accept, in order. |
| `state` | `option<json>` | The protocol state after this arrival; absent leaves it unchanged.  The host uses it for the next call at once, and commits it once every message of this reading is accepted. |
| `frames` | `list<string>` | Text frames to send on the socket now, in order. |
| `acknowledgments` | `list<http-request>` | Protocol acknowledgments to send before acceptance, with no effect beyond confirming receipt.  Answers to this reading's messages are sent only after these complete. |
| `timer` | `option<u32>` | Milliseconds until a `timer` arrival, replacing any pending timer; absent keeps it. Timers end with the socket. |
| `reconnect` | `bool` | Close the socket and start the next read with `read`. |

#### record `file-data`

File bytes for one outgoing message.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The filename without its original directory. |
| `data` | `list<u8>` | The original bytes, encoded by the mapper for transport. |

#### record `outgoing`

Markdown text with at most one file to send.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` | All text to send, in Markdown. |
| `file` | `option<file-data>` | A file to send with this text, if any. |

#### enum `command-kind`

The commands the host understands.

- `session`: List the Sessions, or switch to the one named after it.
- `cancel`: Stop the work of the conversation's Session.
- `backtrack`: Go back to the message the command replies to.
- `everyone`: Open the group to everyone, or close it to the owner only.
- `halt`: Halt the named Session and its descendants, or the conversation's Session when no name
follows.
- `archive`: Archive the named Session and its descendants; with no name, list the Sessions that
can be archived and archive nothing.
- `status`: Show the conversation's Session and its context.
- `compact`: Compact the conversation's history when its Session's next Run starts.
- `clear`: Start the conversation over; its earlier messages stay recorded.

#### record `command`

A command the host understands, as it should appear in the protocol's menus.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `command-kind` | Which command. |
| `description` | `string` | What it does, for the menu. |
| `direct` | `bool` | Whether it applies in private conversations: one-to-one ones, and those in a realm the owner declared private. |
| `group` | `bool` | Whether it applies in group conversations that are not private. |

#### variant `fetch-step`

The next step of fetching the content a locator names.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | `http-request` | Send this request and call again with its response. |
| `download` | `string` | Get this absolute URL taken from the protocol's content and call again with its response.  The host sends it without credentials and only to one of the mapper's `origins`, so content never chooses a path on the service; an address elsewhere makes the attachment unavailable. |
| `file` | `list<u8>` | The bytes of the file an attachment's locator names. |
| `messages` | `list<quoted-message>` | The messages a quote's locator names, listed as `quoted.messages` is. |
| `name` | `string` | The nonempty name a `conversation-name` locator names. |
| `unavailable` | `string` | The protocol refused it for good; the text says why. |

#### record `activity-epilogue`

How a Run turned out, left in place of its view where the view was only for display.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `elapsed-seconds` | `u32` | Seconds the Run took. |
| `rounds` | `u32` | The Rounds it used. |
| `end` | `run-end` | How it ended. |
| `unsent` | `bool` | Whether it finished without sending its last reply. |
| `excerpt` | `string` | The first line of its last reply, sent or not, shortened by the host; empty when it has none. |

#### enum `tool-state`

Where a tool call stands.

- `running`: The call has started and has no settlement yet.
- `ok`: It succeeded.
- `failed`: The call finished with a known failure.
- `unknown`: It may have taken effect, but its result is not known.

#### record `tool-activity`

One tool call shown in an activity view.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The tool's name, as the model calls it. |
| `state` | `tool-state` | Where the call stands. |
| `arguments` | `string` | The values of the call's required arguments in its schema's order, on one line the host shortens; empty when it has none. |

#### record `activity-view`

What the Agent is doing while a Run goes on.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `elapsed-seconds` | `u32` | Seconds since the Run started. |
| `tools` | `list<tool-activity>` | The Run's latest tool calls, oldest first. |

#### variant `activity-update`

What to do with a Run's view.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `view` | `activity-view` | Show or refresh the live view. |
| `epilogue` | `activity-epilogue` | End the view with the Run's epilogue: rewrite the view, or create one when none is shown. |
| `remove` | `_` | Remove the view. |

#### func `origins`

```wit
origins: func() -> list<string>;
```

Additional origins for requests and sockets; `*.` before a host covers its subdomains. Read
when the generation loads.

#### func `pacing`

```wit
pacing: func() -> option<pacing-gap>;
```

The gap before each message `send` builds; absent sends each as soon as it is ready. Read
when the generation loads.

#### func `identify`

```wit
identify: func() -> http-request;
```

The request that reads which account the connection reaches.

#### func `identified`

```wit
identified: func(response: http-response) -> result<identity, fault>;
```

The account in that request's response.

#### func `read`

```wit
read: func(identity: identity, state: option<json>) -> result<read-step, fault>;
```

How to read next, from the latest protocol state; `state` is absent before the protocol
gave one.

`channel.invalid_state` means the state cannot be resumed. The host clears only that
state and retries from `none`, keeping routes and other committed business facts. If the
mapper rejects `none` too, the host stops the connection.

#### func `received`

```wit
received: func(identity: identity, state: option<json>, arrival: arrival) -> result<reading, fault>;
```

What an arrival means, given the latest protocol state.

#### func `fetch`

```wit
fetch: func(locator: string, responses: list<http-response>, limit: u32) -> result<fetch-step, fault>;
```

The next step of fetching the content at `locator`, given the responses so far.

One fetch may send at most `limit` requests and downloads in all; asking for more is a
contract failure.

#### func `split`

```wit
split: func(message: outgoing) -> list<outgoing>;
```

The protocol messages to send, in order; at least one, none empty. Together they carry all
of the message's text and its file, laid out as the protocol needs.

#### func `send`

```wit
send: func(conversation: string, part: outgoing) -> result<http-request, fault>;
```

The request that sends one part to a conversation.

#### func `answered`

```wit
answered: func(response: http-response) -> result<option<string>, fault>;
```

What the protocol answered: the ID of the message a request created, if any, or why it
failed.

A failure with code `channel.conversation_gone` means the conversation no longer exists;
the host forgets its route.

#### func `respond`

```wit
respond: func(handle: string, text: option<string>) -> result<option<http-request>, fault>;
```

The request that answers the accepted message carrying `handle`, showing `text` to its
sender; absent when nothing more needs sending.

#### func `commands`

```wit
commands: func(identity: identity, commands: list<command>) -> list<http-request>;
```

Requests that offer the host's commands in the protocol's menus, sent when a connection
starts.

#### func `activity`

```wit
activity: func(conversation: string, replies-here: bool, shown: option<string>, update: activity-update) -> option<http-request>;
```

Creates, refreshes, rewrites or removes a Run's view; absent when nothing needs sending,
and for a new view when the protocol shows none.

`replies-here` says whether the Run's replies go to `conversation`; otherwise the view is
only for display there. Where they go, create no view when `presence` already shows it.

A view is not a message for the reader's attention: where the protocol allows, create it
without a notification.

The host reads each response with `answered`. When it creates a live view (`view` without
`shown`), it keeps the message ID `answered` gives as `shown`, and without one the Run
shows no view there; an epilogue ends the view, so its ID is not kept.

#### func `presence`

```wit
presence: func(conversation: string, view: activity-view) -> option<http-request>;
```

A passing sign in `conversation` that the Agent is working, such as typing or an expiring
draft of `view`; absent when the protocol has none.

The host sends it only where the Run's replies go, when the Run starts and at each refresh
until it ends, keeps nothing of it, and reads its response with `answered`.

#### func `open-conversation`

```wit
open-conversation: func(beside: string, session: list<string>) -> option<http-request>;
```

The request opening a child Session's own conversation beside `beside`, where its parent
shows; absent when the mapper knows the protocol cannot open one there.

Where the protocol refuses to open one there, `opened` gives that failure and the child is
not shown on this connection. `session` is the child's full name, segment by segment; lay
out the title so that it reads apart from the conversations people open. Opening may leave
the protocol's one-time notice.

#### func `opened`

```wit
opened: func(beside: string, response: http-response) -> result<string, fault>;
```

The nonempty ID of the conversation that an `open-conversation` request made beside
`beside` created, or why it failed.

#### func `close-conversation`

```wit
close-conversation: func(conversation: string) -> option<http-request>;
```

The request that puts away a conversation opened for a child Session once that Session is
archived; absent when nothing needs sending.

For instance, this deletes a topic or archives a thread. The host reads its response with
`answered`.
